drhp.business: ARE&M manufactures automotive and industrial lead-acid batteries under brands like Amaron and Quanta, and is expanding into new energy through lithium-ion cell and pack manufacturing, EV charging, and battery recycling. The company serves OEMs, aftermarket customers, and infrastructure developers across over 70 countries, with a growing focus on energy storage systems and advanced cell technologies.

drhp.expansion: Amara Raja Circular Solutions Private Limited (ARCS), a wholly owned subsidiary, is establishing a battery recycling facility at Cheyyar, Tamil Nadu. Battery Breaker operations commenced during the year and are in ramp-up. Refining operations, which started in H2 2024, continue to scale up. Phase II refinery expansion is underway with commissioning targeted by 2027. Commissioning of the Crystallizer and De-sulphurisation plant is expected shortly. risks.note: ARACT is in early-stage ramp-up with net losses, targeting Start of Production by 2027; delays or cost overruns at the Giga Corridor could impact the strategic pivot to New Energy.
risks.risk: Execution risk in scaling new lithium-ion cell manufacturing

risks.note: Shift from lead-acid to lithium-ion and advanced chemistries (LFP, NMC) exposes the company to technology risk, customer qualification delays, and potential stranded assets in legacy battery segments.
ARCS recycling ramp-up (Phase II refinery, de-sulphurisation) is critical for lead and alloy security. Delays in scaling refining or alloy production could disrupt cost and supply-chain resilience.
risks.risk: Raw material supply and circular-economy integration

risks.note: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) under Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, and evolving environmental norms require continuous investment and operational adaptation, especially for recycling and lead operations.
risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk in battery waste management

risks.note: Automotive and industrial battery segments rely on a concentrated OEM customer base; shifts in OEM procurement strategies or EV adoption rates could materially affect volumes and margins.
Increasing digitalisation across manufacturing, R&D, and customer interfaces elevates exposure to cyber threats, which could disrupt operations or compromise sensitive data.

The company is exposed to tightening climate regulations, carbon pricing, and investor expectations. Failure to meet SBTi or GHG reduction targets could lead to reputational damage and higher cost of capital.

In mobility, ECUs (ISG, EFI, ISG+EFI, EV motor control units) are indispensable to vehicle function; adoption is driven by regulation (emissions/efficiency) and OEM technology transitions, with Tier-I suppliers driving innovation.
